title: Concurrent SQL updates commit a successor hearing before its adjourned parent despite V406
environment: Exact source JAR + disposable PostgreSQL18.6; normal triggers; non-owner NOSUPERUSER/NOCREATEDB/NOCREATEROLE writer with SELECT/UPDATE only
preconditions: Parent hearing2026-01-03 adjourned via API to successor2026-01-06
Two ordinary READ COMMITTED database connections; no disabled integrity triggers
steps: A: BEGIN; UPDATE hearing SET hearing_date='2026-01-05' WHERE id='<parent>'; leave uncommitted
B: BEGIN; UPDATE hearing SET hearing_date='2026-01-04' WHERE id='<successor>'; COMMIT
Fresh SELECT joins successor.adjourned_from_id=parent.id and compares dates
expected: Reject or serialize incompatible writes; zero committed successor dates on/before parent
risk_boundary: Trusted database writer invariant hole. No remote API/authorization bypass asserted. All reproduction SQL confined to disposable QA databases. Original QAD033 parent/date/case probes now pass; this additional linked-hearing race remains.
fix_guidance: Coordinate date checks and writes across both linked hearings with a consistent locking/serialization strategy. Retest both transaction orders, rollback and cancelled/history preservation; avoid deadlocks.

retests.note: Original reproduction and both lock orders prevent invalid commits; expert race,40P01victim rollback,API chronology29 and real V408 upgrade5 pass. No direct UAT SQL fault injection.
